Just... bad. For anyone remotely familiar with computers, this game is cringe-worthy at best. Some weird mix of unix and dos idioms that just don't exist anywhere. The shell is half-assed and inconsistent, and absolutely nothing even closely emulates the real tools which have had their names disgraced. This game might be decent if the file system behaved the way it should, but it does not. In particular:
- wildcards do not work in all commands
- there is no file management beyond rm, mv, and a unicorn scp? can't make directories or copy files on localhost
- devs don't appear to understand how file systems work: ~ and / are used interchangably through the game/tutorial/help docs
- cd can't evaluate more than one step up or down the file tree

some other things to note:
- connections to other systems just don't make sense
- cracking ssh is somehow easier/less resource intensive than screwing with an ftp server? what?
- cat to read files?? really? I smell cat abuse
- no echo?

try again... or don't?

[h1]The Three Virtues[/h1][olist]
[*][b]Laziness: [/b]The quality that makes you go to great effort to reduce overall energy expenditure. It makes you write labor-saving programs that other people will find useful and document what you wrote so you don't have to answer so many questions about it.
[*][b]Impatience:[/b] The anger you feel when the computer is being lazy. This makes you write programs that don't just react to your needs, but actually anticipate them. Or at least pretend to.
[*][b]Hubris:[/b] The quality that makes you write (and maintain) programs that other people won't want to say bad things about.

I was gifted a copy of this game from one of my friends, and boy do I not regret getting this.... The game is subjectively awesome to me IMO. The general story line and text gems you find through hacking is interesting and funny. I don't know much about hacking, but I will say that in an overall context, it does kind of follow the general popularised movie formula for what hacking is.... It forces you to use the keybaord speedily and efficiciently... You can't afford to fumble at certain times. 

You also have to think like a "hacker".... SOMETIMES you need to be able to make "connections" & see the links that make up the puzzle in order to figure out how to get to the answer... You have to learn to optimise your "workflow" and computer memory at times to do things fast or find a way for you to be able to take your time..

The game felt fairly forgiving to me in terms of being "slow" or "fumbling" at the keyboard, as a reference, I have a general score of 51WPM with an accuracy of 95.1% from [url=http://play.typeracer.com/] this site[/url] to help you gauge where you might fall. While you shouldn't be generally typing out full words, the speed at which you can process comes into play. I have had previous experience working in old DOS and in programming for fun, but don't be intimidated from playing. Seriously...

Hacknet, to me, is to hacking like what the phrase "this is what a rabbit hole looks like and here's how you find it", is to Alice In Wonderland. If you can understand it.... If you have any kind of interest in hacking or just want to feel that "rush" of hacking, then I highly recommend you PLAY THIS GAME. It's so fun I will play it again just to see what else I can "see" or achieve...

An interesting mix between Uplink and Street Hacker, for the price of ~10 USD is definitely worth checking out.

The game is pretty fun, some things require attention to detail and logical thinking, and the humor is pretty good!

However, the game launched with a very bad bug which might make your save useless: if you try to make two missions at a time, you won't be able to complete the first one. This can simply kill your save.
Also, even though the presentation is well done and the interface looks pretty, I don't see much advance over what other Hacking games did before (Uplink was released in 2001), so you really should approach this with caution. The biggest difference here is being able to use both a GUI and a Console - which is good news.

This doesn't detract from the enjoyment of the game, of course. But it does dissapoint if you expected anything more than that.

I haven't finished the game yet, due to the bug that probably broke my savegame. But about the plot: it's decently intriguing and will make you want to uncover all the secrets, as a hacking game should.

So even though I ended up pretty disappointed - it's 2015, yet there's little news here. Even Street Hacker, which is a decade old and terribly programmed, had deeper features; and Uplink had a more compelling gameplay and story - there's still some fun to be had and some jokes/moments actually made me laugh or smile. 
I do recommend waiting for a patch before playing it, though. So rush it on your own risk.

Puzzles, reading, stress management... All in all, it's a fun and challenging game. Also a frustrating and annoying game. It sort of depends on your mood and attitude. There were times I was caught up by the puzzles and the challenges, and times where I wanted to throw my computer across the room. Then finally I caved in, looked at a guide and wanted to punch myself for not having seen the obvious solution for the problem. 

So, playwise, it's a fun game.

I feel like there are too few tools. You learn to use a few tools and programs, but after the first 5 that's it, and you just solve the problems with the tools you have. For a better game: More tools.

Then there's the netmap, which is... horrible. The servers you connect to pop up somewhere random, and you can't hide the ones you don't need, so eventually the map is cluttered, confusing and worthless. I ended up with a notepad with the needed ip adresses beside me. 

So, some things could be better, a lot of things could be worse. I'd recommend the game for people who like finding solutions to puzzles, quizzes and riddles. Creative thinkers who can digest a lot of text in a short amount of time (scan the text more so than read it), and who can handle flashing lights and preassure. I don't recommend it for the first person shooters, young kids (not that it's violent, I just don't think they'd be entertained much) or for light gaming where you're partially talking to your girlfriend, partially on facebook and partially gaming. It's not good for those types of situations.
If you want to try the very tip of hacking this game might help you get that fix. Kudos to the development team for creating such a great game! Highly recommended if you're into cyber-crime!

Hacknet is an interesting game. Let's just get that out of the way. Its got a very good storyline and, while I have some experience in [strike]hacking[/strike] computer security, I didn't find (most) of the puzzles too difficult for the average person to solve. It sets a very good pace, picking up the difficulty very well. I'm writing this review just after completing the game, which took me just over 6 hours.

You start off with a message from Bit, telling you how to use the Hacknet software, etc. etc. Basically a tutorial on how to use it, the command line, that sort of thing. (If you're a linux user, this game will be much easier, the commands are basically the same for navigating the terminal and the like) After this, you're sent off to a hacker group, Entropy. You do a few hacks, and things start to pick up. You rise to the top (naturally) and start going off, investigating. I'd say more but I don't want to risk spoilers. The ending was very intriguing, and worth the effort.

The challenges are similar, but I never got bored of them. Find server at X IP, break down any proxies, firewalls, and open ports to use the almighty PortHack and get the admin password. Then, do whatever you need to, be it uploading or downloading a file, deleting stuff, or (later) even messing with databases and some... other devices. ([spoiler]a pacemaker[/spoiler]) They become more difficult as you progress, adding tracers that initiate an IP change failsafe if you take too long, more ports to open, and more complex firewalls and proxies. You'll need to grab passwords from emails and circumvent servers with powerful tracers, and even more interesting events. The only randomly difficult challenge that jumped me was an attack on my PC, which I was able to avoid using a [spoiler]trap shell[/spoiler]. If it gets you, there is a guide to help you out.

The interface is very intuitive and I never had any unreasonable issues with it, aside from becoming stuck when entering a password I didn't want to enter. (Which is my fault, I clicked login. What did I expect?) Later, you get the option to switch your layout, but none of them are really terrible. You have the terminal window (for commands), the display window (for showing the filesystem, passwords, databases, emails, etc.), the RAM window (watch this one, especially later when you get more RAM-hungry programs), and your NetMap (showing all the IPs you've connected to/can connect to).

The playtime was a good length. I would have liked it to be a bit longer but 6 hours is longer than AAA campaigns. God I hate AAA companies. Be innovative. Or I'll use Hacknet to take down your servers. /rant. Anyway, I'm not complaining about the length. As I said earlier, it never got repetitive, it was always interesting. There was always a sense of "oh gotta do this quickly or they're gonna catch me with that trace" that pushes you forward. Because of that speed though, don't play this game if you're not a quick typist. I have a speed of about 70 WPM (Faster now), which is well above average. I'd recommend being able to go above 40 WPM to play this effectively. 

------------------------------------------------------

Of course, what's a review without a pro/con list.

Pros:
+Good, interesting gameplay
+Active modding community (for extra levels and whatnot)
+Great value for the price (Yes, I know I got it for $2.99. But it's worth the full $9.99)
+Nice visuals (watch out, 1 looks like lowercase L. Tripped me up once)
+Easter Egg bash.org quotes
+Amazing soundtrack. Reflects the mood and urgency of the situations. 10/10 on that.

Neutrals:
+-Console window pops up behind game (Alt Tabbing is a little wierd)
+-Can't skip ending credits

Cons:
-You need to be a quick and accurate typist
-Requires some prior knowledge of terminal commands in order to be efficient (from the start)

------------------------------------------------------

TL; DR

Very interesting, non-repetitive gameplay and a good storyline. Visuals are of high quality and the soundtrack is amazing. However, to be good at this game you should be good at typing ( >40 WPM) and know how to navigate the Linux terminal, or at least pick up on it quickly. (I mean, it's just ls, cd, cat, and mv really) Also, bash.org quotes.

I've just finished the Hacknet: Labyrinths DLC. I'm adding a short little note here about that.

Definetely worth it. Took an extra 3 and a half hours or so to complete, so pretty decent playtime. Much more interesing puzzles than the base game. You are tasked with completing the "Kaguya Trials" from the CSEC list, and join with a group of 3 other hackers. You'll take missions from a list and complete them with the help of the others. While you usually never actually interact with them other than seeing them in the IRC, it does feel like they're helping you. (I won't spoil how, but it becomes apparent in the endgame.) The challenges were a bit more difficult, but nothing that wasn't impossible. A mission towards the end just becomes a cat-and-mouse chase for a password, but while it didn't seem to guide you it wasn't that difficult to follow the clues. Overall, I'd highly rate the DLC. If you have the extra cash when buying Hacknet, I would recommend purchasing it. Do complete it after the main game though, or your NetMap will become a mess...

------------------------------------------------------
